Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal PM Balen Shah | Photo Credit: AP
The Prime Minister of Nepal, Balendra Shah , arrived in New Delhi on Sunday (November 22, 2026) afternoon for his first official visit to India. The Prime Ministers of both the countries inaugurated the Saryu-Kamala rail service from Ayodhya to Janakpur, Nepal and Dharchula road bridge between Uttarakhand and Nepal, through video conferencing.
Also read | Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
According to sources, Monday’s (November 23, 2026) discussion between the two Prime Ministers will give “political direction” to bilateral relations for the coming years.
Also read | Nepal’s plea at climate summit reveals limits of loss and damage finance
Mr. Shah is leading a 34-member delegation that includes his Chief Advisor Kumar Byanjankar, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Minister for Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal. A separate business delegation is also visiting India along with the Prime Minister’s delegation.
“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.
PM Modi announced that India will establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Nepal, alongside a startup incubator and an innovation hub, as part of a broader push to empower Nepali youth and deepen bilateral educational and technological cooperation.
“Friends, Nepal’s youth generation is full of talent, energy, and big dreams. India is fully committed to partnering in making their dreams a reality. To realise this resolve, we will establish a startup incubator, an innovation hub, and an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal,” PM Modi said.
Alongside setting up the IIT offshore campus, the Prime Minister announced expanded academic avenues in India for students from the Himalayan nation, stating, “We will expand scholarship opportunities in India for Nepali students in law and technology.”
Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties.
Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah warmly welcomed Indian investors to Nepal and called for translating bilateral understandings and infrastructure milestones into tangible gains for farmers, youth, students, and entrepreneurs across both countries.
“We are clear that the outcomes of the understandings that we reached today, and the projects we advance, must translate into prosperity in the fields of our farmers, employment and opportunity in the hands of our youth, new horizons in the dreams of our students, and tangible avenues for new markets, investment, and business expansion for our entrepreneurs. I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to stand on the sturdy foundation of this enduring bond,” he added.
India will establish an offshore campus of IIT, expand scholarship opportunities in Law and Technology for Nepali students in India, says PM Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored New Delhi’s role in keeping fuel, fertiliser, and other essentials flowing to Nepal under its “Neighbourhood First” approach despite supply pressures this year.
“In keeping with our ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy, despite severe challenges in oil supply this year, we maintained uninterrupted supplies of fuel, fertiliser, and other essential goods to Nepal. Today, the dedication of Phase II of the Motihari–Amlekhgunj pipeline and the foundation stone laying for the Jhapa petroleum terminal will further strengthen this partnership,” he stated.
The energy and fuel initiatives were unveiled alongside a Joint Vision Document aimed at advancing shared goals of “Viksit Bharat” and “Samunnat Nepal” he added.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted clean hydropower and uninterrupted fuel and essential supplies as key pillars of Nepal’s economic growth, pointing to the groundbreaking for the Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project, commitments on Arun-3, and expanding cross-border petroleum infrastructure during talks with visiting Nepalese PM Balendra Shah.
“Friends, the rivers of Nepal have immense potential for clean energy. India’s vast energy market can make these possibilities a strong foundation for Nepal’s economic prosperity. Today’s groundbreaking for the Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project and our commitment to complete Arun-3 on time are part of this vision,” PM Modi said.
Linking cultural storytelling with youth and sports exchanges, the Prime Minister noted that shared narratives such as the Ramayana are reaching global audiences through modern formats.
“Friends, today, the story of the Ramayana is reaching the new generation and the entire world through films and modern technology. We want young creators from India and Nepal to come together and present our shared heritage to the world through new media. In this direction, we will welcome a large delegation from Nepal at the upcoming WAVES summit. In sports, especially in cricket, we will increase our cooperation in developing infrastructure and training players in Nepal,” he said.
As part of efforts to deepen cultural, religious, and people-to-people ties between the two countries, a new cross-border road bridge linking Uttarakhand and Nepal was inaugurated by the Prime Ministers of India and Nepal.
“Friends, today, we inaugurated the Dharchula road bridge between Uttarakhand and Nepal, and laid the foundation stone for the Integrated Check Post at Banbasa. Along with this, on the Nepal side, we will also rapidly advance the work on the Dodhara Chandani Integrated Check Post. Through these initiatives, trade and the movement of people between Uttarakhand and Nepal will become even more convenient,” PM Modi said.
Prime Minister Modi, speaking on the inaugural of the Saryu-Kamala train service, said, “Friends, the relations between India and Nepal are woven with threads of shared history, faith, culture, and deep people-to-people ties. Lord Ram and Mother Sita are the symbols of our shared civilisation and faith. In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said: without Nepal, our dhams are incomplete; without Nepal, our Ram is also incomplete”.
Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad termed his non-invitation to the launch of the direct Ayodhya-Janakpur train service an insult to the people of Ayodhya, saying they had elected him as their representative from the Faizabad Lok Sabha constituency.
Mr. Prasad said he was neither informed over the phone nor sent an invitation card for the event, despite the significance of the project connecting Ayodhya Dham with Janakpur.
Welcoming the initiative, he congratulated the Prime Ministers of India and Nepal on the launch of the train service.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India maintained supply of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year.
India and Nepal are partners in each other’s progress and source of support for each other in difficult times, he said.
The relationship between the two countries is not merely that of neighbours, but is reflective of unbreakable trust and friendship, he added.
Describing the rail service as a gift that would bring Awadh and Mithila closer, Mr. Adityanath extended his heartfelt congratulations to devotees of Lord Ram.
Nepal PM Balendra Shah said the talks between the two countries were aimed at further strengthening and modernising centuries-old Nepal-India ties.
As dependable neighbour, India consistently stood as first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult time in Nepal, he added.
Mr. Shah also said ties between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal today in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods.
“To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees,” Mr. Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.
Nepal and India are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in various sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation. Beyond Government-level engagements, the visit will also feature a Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal.
Saryu-Kamala Express, which will run between Ayodhya and Janakpur, Nepal, was inaugurated today at the Ayodhya Cantt Railway Station via video conferencing by PM Narendra Modi and Nepal PM Balen Shah.
Nepal PM Balendra Shah after paying homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat today, wrote in the memorial’s visitor book describing truth as “a power unmatched by any force” and calling compassion “the ultimate strength”.
Linking Gandhi’s legacy with Nepal’s heritage, the Nepalese PM added, “On behalf of the people and Government of Nepal, I offer my deepest tribute. Coming from the birthplace of Lord Buddha, I behold in Gandhiji’s legacy that very same immortal light: the profound truth that compassion is the ultimate strength, and that true leadership lies in selfless service to the humblest among us.”
The Ministry of External Affairs said, “India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports”.
Prime Minister Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of his Nepalese counterpart and his 34-member government delegation.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the start of a direct rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur in Nepal will open a new chapter in the centuries-old spiritual and cultural ties between the two regions and would strengthen India-Nepal relations and facilitate pilgrimage for crores of devotees.
India and Nepal discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.
Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit. The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation.
Former Nepal PM Jhala Nath Khanal said Nepal and India should maintain cordial relations and expand comprehensive cooperation, while expressing concern that Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah had not prepared a common national agenda ahead of his ongoing visit to India.
“There are many expectations. And there are some irritants also in our relations which have to be eliminated. And the relations between our two countries should be comprehensively developed based on five principles of peaceful coexistence and neighbourliness,” Mr. Khanal said.
While Nepal’s new Government may be granted some leeway for early misspeaking, Kathmandu and Delhi must tread carefully in their words and steps. Any indication from Kathmandu that it is cavalier about India’s position in the region, or from Delhi that it seeks to interfere with the new Government’s working, could set off the same cycles of mistrust that have dogged the relationship, particularly since the Nepal Constitution friction and trade blockade from India in 2015.
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah has proposed establishing a Himalayan Climate Resilience Mechanism led by his country as well as India and China, in the wake of the recent devastating flash floods in the area.
Mr. Shah, in his maiden address to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on Thursday (September 24, 2026), also told world leaders that a warming climate is destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology.
As Bangladesh and Nepal hold crucial elections — on February 12, 2026, and March 5, 2026, respectively — following dramatic youth-led uprisings, the outcomes will be closely watched, for they will not only reshape domestic politics in the two countries but also impact regional dynamics. Speaking to The Hindu , Roman Gautam , Editor of Himal Southasian , reflects on the political churn in the region, India’s role, and the prospects for regional cooperation.
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah “Balen” limited his intervention in a parliamentary discussion on the boundary dispute between India and Nepal over Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura (areas claimed by both countries) on May 31 to a few minutes. He seemed to suggest that the issue was not one-sided.
Nepal's Prime Minister advocates for a rational resolution to the India-Nepal boundary dispute, signaling a new diplomatic phase.
Former Nepal Foreign Minister Pradeep Kumar Gyawali has said that Prime Minister Balen Shah’s maiden visit to India should focus on addressing the trust deficit between the two neighbouring countries and resolving long-pending bilateral issues.
He also expressed concern over the lack of consultations with political parties and the President ahead of the visit, describing the approach as unprecedented.
Speaking to ANI on Sunday, Mr. Gyawali said, “He has not held any consultations with political parties, and he has not even informed the President about this state visit. This is an unprecedented approach... We hope that he will raise issues of concern to Nepal. Most importantly, since the events of last September—followed by new elections and the formation of a new government—a sense of distance and a ‘trust deficit’ have emerged between Delhi and Kathmandu. Therefore, he should focus on bridging this gap and restoring trust between these two vital neighbouring partner nations.”
On the eve of Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s official visit to India, the Nepali Congress, the country’s main opposition party, has urged the government to put national interest first, adding that this will help make the trip “successful and productive”.
Nepali Congress party’s senior vice president Bishwa Prakash Sharma, in a statement, said the visit should serve Nepal’s best interests while further strengthening ties between the two countries.
“Nepal-India relations should be grounded in mutual respect, sovereign equality, and national interest,” the party said.
The Prime Minister of Nepal, Balendra Shah, arrived in New Delhi on Sunday (November 22, 2026) afternoon for his first official visit to India. Sources said that Mr. Shah will inaugurate several projects on Monday and is scheduled to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Nepal PM Balendra Shah visits Delhi for first official talks with Modi, signaling years of enhanced bilateral ties and major development projects.
